name: Greenplum
tagline: PostgreSQL-based MPP data warehouse, closed-sourced by Broadcom in 2024 and sold in Tanzu Data.
description: Greenplum is a shared-nothing MPP warehouse that shards PostgreSQL across many segment hosts, adding a parallel optimizer (GPORCA), append-optimized columnar tables and external tables for parallel loading. Pivotal open-sourced it in 2015, but after Broadcom acquired VMware it closed the source in May 2024 and archived the public repositories; Tanzu Greenplum 7 (on PostgreSQL 12) continues as a commercial product inside the Tanzu Data suite. Existing customers get a capable, Postgres-familiar MPP system; the open-source community moved to forks such as Apache Cloudberry.
statusNote: Broadcom closed the source in May 2024 and archived the public GitHub repos; development continues only as commercial Tanzu Greenplum. Open fork: Apache Cloudberry.

pricing.notes: Sold as part of the VMware Tanzu Data suite under Broadcom subscriptions.

scale.notes: Shared-nothing segments with mirrors; scales by adding segment hosts and redistributing data.

strengths: PostgreSQL SQL, drivers and tools with MPP parallelism
GPORCA cost-based optimizer for complex analytic queries
Append-optimized row and column tables with compression
Parallel loading via external tables and gpfdist
In-database analytics with MADlib, PostGIS and procedural languages
weaknesses: Closed source since 2024; community and ecosystem largely moved on
Tied to Broadcom's Tanzu bundling and pricing
Based on an older PostgreSQL version
Expansion and rebalancing are heavy operations
